title: An iterative method bridging DFT, disorder averaging, and experiment in intercalated materials: application to Au-intercalated graphene
authors: Poonam Kumari, Alberto Zobelli, Igor de Melo Froldi, Adeline Crepieux, Laurent Simon, Cristina Bena
abstract: Intercalation can strongly modify the electronic dispersion of a host material, as directly revealed by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). We develop a general iterative method combining density functional theory (DFT), tight-binding (TB), disorder averaging within the self-consistent T-matrix approximation (SCTMA), and experiment, to construct an effective model of the intercalated system. DFT identifies the relevant microscopic degrees of freedom and constrains selected model parameters, while comparison of SCTMA calculations with experiment guides their further refinement. We apply this method to graphene intercalated with Au clusters and show that it reproduces the main ARPES signatures of the Au-cluster phase, including the broadening of the V12an Hove singularity and the emergence of kink-like features in the dispersion. The essential microscopic ingredients identified by the analysis are the hybridization between selected intercalant orbitals and the graphene states, together with an intercalation-induced local scattering potential.
summary: This work introduces an iterative method that combines DFT, Tight-Binding models, and the Self-Consistent T-matrix Approximation (SCTMA) to model intercalated graphene. By applying this to Au-intercalated graphene, the authors successfully reproduce key ARPES features like VHS broadening and kinks. This demonstrates a robust computational pathway for understanding how impurities modify electronic band structures in disordered 2D materials.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a general, iterative computational framework to accurately model the electronic structure of intercalated materials by bridging theoretical calculations (DFT/TB) with disorder averaging techniques and experimental ARPES data.
main_result: The method successfully reproduces key ARPES signatures for Au-intercalated graphene, identifying that hybridization between specific Au orbitals and graphene states, alongside a local scattering potential, are the essential microscopic ingredients governing band structure modification.
method: A multi-step iterative approach is used: DFT determines initial parameters; Wannierization generates an effective Tight-Binding (TB) model; disorder averaging is performed using the Self-Consistent T-matrix Approximation (SCTMA); and finally, results are refined by comparison with ARPES measurements.
model_or_system: The system studied is graphene intercalated with Au clusters. The theoretical framework involves an effective TB Hamiltonian incorporating hybridization terms ($\hat{H}_{	ext{hyb}}$) between the host $\pi$ bands and localized orbitals from the intercalant, alongside a local potential term ($U$).
key_observables: Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) spectral function $A(\mathbf{k}, \omega)$, specifically observing the broadening of the van Hove singularity (VHS) and the emergence of kink-like features in the dispersion.
important_parameters: The analysis requires tuning parameters such as hybridization amplitudes ($|t_\alpha|$), the local potential strength ($U$), and the impurity density ($n_{	ext{imp}}$) to match experimental linewidths and energy shifts.
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include neglecting substrate effects (SiC), assuming random/dilute distribution of intercalants (justifying SCTMA), and treating certain environmental interactions (like local potential $U$) phenomenologically rather than deriving them purely from DFT.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow, showing initial DFT dispersion plots, and final results comparing the calculated disorder-averaged spectral function via SCTMA against experimental ARPES data along high-symmetry paths ($\Gamma	ext{K}\Gamma$).
paper_structure: The paper follows a logical progression: first establishing the need for an integrated method; second, detailing the DFT/Wannierization steps to build the initial TB model; third, implementing SCTMA to handle disorder averaging; and finally, applying this full pipeline to Au-graphene to extract physical parameters that match experimental observations.
why_interesting: The methodology represents a powerful example of combining multiple advanced computational techniques (DFT, Wannierization, T-matrix theory) into a single predictive framework for complex condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for modeling engineered quantum materials.
